# hexwrap

Helpers for a board game played on a hexagonal map that wraps around on both axes (a torus).

## Coordinates

Cells are addressed in **odd-r offset coordinates**: `Hex{col, row}` with rows running down. Hexes are "pointy-top", and every
**odd** row is shifted half a cell to the right. A `Map(w, h)` has `w` columns and `h` rows; `h` must be even (so that the shifted
rows line up when the map wraps vertically). The constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` unless `w >= 1` and `h >= 2` and `h`
is even.

Any `col` and `row` (negative or large) are accepted by the methods below and are first reduced into the map with `wrap`: `col` modulo `w` and
`row` modulo `h`, always into `0 <= col < w`, `0 <= row < h` (`-1` becomes `w - 1` / `h - 1`). Results are always in that canonical form.

## Directions

`enum Dir { E, NE, NW, W, SW, SE }` (values 0..5, in this order). From a cell `(col, row)` the neighbour in each direction is:

| direction | even row | odd row |
|---|---|---|
| E  | `(col+1, row)`   | `(col+1, row)` |
| W  | `(col-1, row)`   | `(col-1, row)` |
| NE | `(col, row-1)`   | `(col+1, row-1)` |
| NW | `(col-1, row-1)` | `(col, row-1)` |
| SE | `(col, row+1)`   | `(col+1, row+1)` |
| SW | `(col-1, row+1)` | `(col, row+1)` |

The parity is that of the (wrapped) row of the cell you start from. The neighbour is then wrapped. On small maps two directions can lead to the same cell.

## `class Map`

* `Hex wrap(Hex h) const`; `int index(Hex h) const` (row-major index `row * w + col` of the wrapped cell); `Hex from_index(int i) const`.
* `std::array<Hex, 6> neighbors(Hex h) const`: the six neighbours in direction order `E, NE, NW, W, SW, SE` (duplicates stay in place).
* `Hex step(Hex h, Dir d, int n) const`: move `n` cells in direction `d`, one neighbour step at a time (the row parity is re-evaluated
  after every step); a negative `n` moves in the opposite direction (`d + 3 mod 6`) `-n` times. `n == 0` returns the wrapped `h`.
  `std::invalid_argument` when `|n| > 10000`.
* `int distance(Hex a, Hex b) const`: the number of neighbour steps of a shortest route, taking the wrap-around into account. Without wrapping, the
  distance is computed in cube coordinates: `x = col - (row - (row & 1)) / 2`, `z = row`, `y = -x - z`, and the distance is
  `max(|dx|, |dy|, |dz|)`. On the torus the distance is the smallest of these over the nine copies of `b` shifted by `(i*w, j*h)` for
  `i, j` in `{-1, 0, 1}` (both `a` and `b` are wrapped first).
* `std::vector<Hex> within(Hex center, int radius) const`: every distinct cell of the map whose distance from `center` is `<= radius`, sorted by row, then
  by column. A negative radius gives an empty list.
* `std::vector<Hex> ring(Hex center, int radius) const`: the cells at distance exactly `radius`, sorted the same way. `ring(c, 0)` is `{c}`; a
  negative radius gives an empty list.
* `int region_size(Hex start, const std::vector<bool> &blocked) const`: the number of cells reachable from `start` by neighbour steps without entering a blocked
  cell, `start` included. `blocked` is indexed by `index`; its size must be `w * h` (`std::invalid_argument` otherwise). A blocked `start` gives 0.

# hexwrap

Helpers for a board game played on a hexagonal map that wraps around on both axes (a torus).

## Coordinates

Cells are addressed in **odd-r offset coordinates**: `Hex{col, row}` with rows running down. Hexes are "pointy-top", and every
**odd** row is shifted half a cell to the right. A `Map(w, h)` has `w` columns and `h` rows; `h` must be even (so that the shifted
rows line up when the map wraps vertically). The constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` unless `w >= 1` and `h >= 2` and `h`
is even.

Any `col` and `row` (negative or large) are accepted by the methods below and are first reduced into the map with `wrap`: `col` modulo `w` and
`row` modulo `h`, always into `0 <= col < w`, `0 <= row < h` (`-1` becomes `w - 1` / `h - 1`). Results are always in that canonical form.

## Directions

`enum Dir { E, NE, NW, W, SW, SE }` (values 0..5, in this order). From a cell `(col, row)` the neighbour in each direction is:

| direction | even row | odd row |
|---|---|---|
| E  | `(col+1, row)`   | `(col+1, row)` |
| W  | `(col-1, row)`   | `(col-1, row)` |
| NE | `(col, row-1)`   | `(col+1, row-1)` |
| NW | `(col-1, row-1)` | `(col, row-1)` |
| SE | `(col, row+1)`   | `(col+1, row+1)` |
| SW | `(col-1, row+1)` | `(col, row+1)` |

The parity is that of the (wrapped) row of the cell you start from. The neighbour is then wrapped. On small maps two directions can lead to the same cell.

## `class Map`

* `Hex wrap(Hex h) const`; `int index(Hex h) const` (row-major index `row * w + col` of the wrapped cell); `Hex from_index(int i) const`.
* `std::array<Hex, 6> neighbors(Hex h) const`: the six neighbours in direction order `E, NE, NW, W, SW, SE` (duplicates stay in place).

  `i, j` in `{-1, 0, 1}` (both `a` and `b` are wrapped first).
* `std::vector<Hex> within(Hex center, int radius) const`: every distinct cell of the map whose distance from `center` is `<= radius`, sorted by row, then
  by column. A negative radius gives an empty list.
* `std::vector<Hex> ring(Hex center, int radius) const`: the cells at distance exactly `radius`, sorted the same way. `ring(c, 0)` is `{c}`; a
  negative radius gives an empty list.

  cell, `start` included. `blocked` is indexed by `index`; its size must be `w * h` (`std::invalid_argument` otherwise). A blocked `start` gives 0.
